**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/05/25 (Thu) 05:10  
[USER] User inquired about tips for choosing the best type of sunscreen for people with sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended looking for sunscreen with physical blockers like zinc oxide and titanium dioxide as they deflect UV rays away from the skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested checking for fragrance-free and hypoallergenic products to avoid allergic reactions or rashes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised finding a higher SPF for more protection against sunburn.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended picking a lotion or cream formula rather than sprays or powders for sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested doing a patch test before using sunscreen to check for negative reactions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised consulting with a dermatologist to find the best product for skin type, tone, and sensitivity level.  
[USER] Asked how often to reapply sunscreen if having sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended reapplying sunscreen every two hours or as directed on the product label.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Mentioned that if swimming or sweating, reapplication may be needed more often.  
[USER] Expressed appreciation for the information.  
[USER] Inquired about what to do if still getting a sunburn despite using sunscreen for sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested cooling the skin with a cool bath or compresses.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended applying a moisturizing lotion or aloe vera to soothe and hydrate the burned skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised taking over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen or ibuprofen for pain relief.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested staying out of the sun until the skin has fully healed.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended consulting a doctor if the sunburn is severe or accompanied by other symptoms like fever or blistering.  
[USER] Asked if mixing different types of sunscreen is advisable for better protection on sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stated it is not recommended to mix different types of sunscreen as it can negate protective benefits and may cause irritation.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Advised using the same brand and type of sunscreen for reapplication.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested consulting with a dermatologist for the best type of sunscreen for sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended patch testing a new sunscreen before use.  
[USER] Inquired if regular body lotion can be used as a substitute for sunscreen on sensitive skin.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Stated it is not recommended to use regular body lotion as a substitute for sunscreen as
